# Workbook mapping — all seven operational tabs

**Every table below was generated by reading `src/forms/registry.ts`**, not transcribed
from the PRD. The row-4 headers in the "Verified row-4 header" column are the
`sheetHeader` values the registry holds, which `docs/workbook-verification.md` records as
having been read from the live spreadsheet on **2026-10-24** with **zero divergence from
the PRD** across all 98 headers.

Regenerate and diff this document against the registry whenever a column changes. The
registry is the single source of truth; this file is a derived view and can go stale.

---

## 1. The workbook contract

Spreadsheet: `BFF-FRM-06_18_Sample_Test_Log_DRAFT` — a **native Google Sheet**.

> The verified spreadsheet is a **DRAFT owned by a personal Gmail account** and must
> **never** be the write target. See `docs/open-decisions.md` D-07. The spreadsheet id is
> the Edge Function secret `SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID`, which has **no default anywhere**: if
> it is unset, the sync worker refuses to run.

### Nine tabs, exact names

| # | Tab name | Role | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Read me` | **Reference. Never written.** | — |
| 2 | `Limits` | **Reference. Never written.** 34 entries, **0 approved.** | A4:I38 |
| 3 | `1 Raw materials` | Operational | A:S (19) |
| 4 | `2 Ground` | Operational | A:AN (40) |
| 5 | `3 Conditioned` | Operational | A:M (13) |
| 6 | `4 Pellets` | Operational | A:K (11) |
| 7 | `5 Extruded soya` | Operational | A:P (16) |
| 8 | `6 Crumble` | Operational | A:AM (39) |
| 9 | `7 Mash` | Operational | A:AJ (36) |

`REFERENCE_TABS = ['Read me', 'Limits']`. The writer refuses to address either, and
`tests/sheetSync.test.ts` derives that assertion from the constant rather than
hardcoding the names.

### Row structure — rows 1 to 4 are PROTECTED

```
 row 1   title                                      ─┐
 row 2   instruction text                            │  PROTECTED_HEADER_ROWS = 4
 row 3   MERGED SECTION-BAND ROW                     │  the writer never addresses
         "Sample details | Settings when sampled |   │  any of these rows
          Test results | Follow-up"                  │
 row 4   COLUMN HEADERS  ← verified verbatim        ─┘
 row 5   first data row                                 FIRST_DATA_ROW = 5
  …
 row 304 end of the template's validation / formatting
```

Three rules follow, and all three are enforced in code:

1. **Row 3 is a merged band row, not data.** The four band labels map one-to-one onto the
   PRD §3.2 form sections and onto the registry's `SECTIONS`
   (`sample_details`, `settings`, `test_results`, `follow_up`). The form renders a band
   only when the stage has applicable fields in it — tabs 1, 4 and 7 therefore show no
   *Settings when sampled* band.
2. **Data starts at row 5.** `FIRST_DATA_ROW = 5`.
3. **The 304-row template is not a ceiling.** PRD NFR-007 forbids assuming a 300-row
   maximum; nothing in the app does. The template's data validation and conditional
   formatting stop at 304, which is a workbook-formatting fact, not an application limit.

### Writing rules

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `valueInputOption = 'RAW'` always | `USER_ENTERED` would evaluate formulas, coerce dates, drop leading zeros and turn a phone number into an arithmetic error. `SHEETS_VALUE_INPUT_OPTION` is a constant and a test asserts the writer agrees with it. |
| Zero is written; blank is left blank | `0` is a measured value, `undefined` is "not measured". Never interchangeable. |
| Entered precision is preserved | `12.50` keeps its trailing zero. Inputs stay uncontrolled for exactly this reason. |
| Coded values become workbook labels | `corn` → `Corn`, `yes` → `Yes`. The code is persisted; the label is written. |
| Non-applicable columns are left untouched | An AM ground sample never writes column L. |
| Formula-like text is neutralised on CSV export | `escapeForCsvExport`; `looksLikeFormula` strips leading whitespace and control characters first, because a tab before `=` still parses as a formula downstream. |
| Headers verified before every write pass | A mismatch fails closed with no API call. |

### Requiredness vocabulary

"Required" means *required for that workflow stage*, never required to save a draft
(PRD §5 preamble, FR-005).

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Server-assigned. Column A only. Never operator-editable. |
| `registration` | Needed to leave Draft and be issued a sample ID. |
| `testing` | Needed to move Awaiting Results → Ready for Review. |
| `review` | Needed to record a review outcome. |
| `optional` | Never required. |

### Reading the Notes column

- **hard bounds** are physical or logical impossibilities — a negative mass, a percentage
  above 100. Violations are **rejected**. They are *not* acceptance limits.
- **typo guard** (`implausibleAbove`) is a soft data-entry guard. The UI asks the operator
  to confirm and then accepts the value exactly as typed. It **never** contributes to a
  conformity assessment and never fails validation.
- **unit NOT confirmed** means the workbook states no approved unit. Such a measurement
  can never be assessed as conforming (UAT-07, R-02).
- A **parameter key** is what links a measurement to a specification rule. A field with no
  parameter key is **recorded only** and can never be assessed.

> No numeric acceptance limit appears anywhere below, or anywhere in the codebase. The
> bounds shown are impossibility checks and typo guards. Acceptance limits live in
> `specification_versions` and require two-person approval.

**0038 changed this tab.** `Urease (pH rise)`, a 3-dp number against an unapproved
0.05–0.20 band, became `Qualitative urease` — the plant runs the visual urea-phenol-red
test, which has no number in it, and asking for one invited the operator to copy a figure
off the reference card that belongs to the quantitative buffer method. `Protein solubility
(%)` was removed at the plant's request; `Tested by (QO)` and `Comments` slid left from O
and P. Neither removed column held a value in the database or in the workbook. See
`docs/workbook-restructure-0038.md` and migration `0038_qualitative_urease.sql`.
`extruded_soya.urease` and `extruded_soya.protein_solubility` remain in
`specification_parameters` as unapproved drafts that nothing can now cite.

formula-injection handling.

## 10. The sample ID

```
    AP  -  2026-10-24  -  01
    │        │             └── sequence within that prefix and that plant-local date
    │        └─────────────── the plant-LOCAL collection date (America/Guyana)
    └──────────────────────── the stage prefix; AM or BC for Ground, by the
                              structured sampling-point code — never by
                              substring-matching display text
```

The sequence key is the plant-local collection date, so a sample collected at 21:00 in
Guyana on the 24th belongs to the 24th even though UTC has already rolled over.
`tests/sampleId.test.ts` and `tests/time.test.ts` cover the format, the parse and the day
boundaries.

## 11. The `Limits` tab

34 entries, **0 of 34 approved.** The full table — every Tab / Sample / Test / Unit / Low
/ High / Status value — is in `docs/workbook-verification.md` §5 and is **not duplicated
here**, because a second copy of a number is a second thing to keep right.

Status breakdown as read on 2026-10-24: 27 *To set*, 4 *Set*, 2 *Confirm with Polinutri*,
1 *To set with Polinutri*. The 4 *Set* rows are **Polinutri vendor reference values** from
a visit on 23 October 2026, **not Bounty Farm approvals**. They are imported as
`status = 'reference_only'` with `approved_by` and `proposed_by` NULL, and they can never
decide conformity.

> `Limits` row 2 warns: *"Do not add, delete or move rows, because the test tabs read
> these cells by their position."* **No rule in this system is keyed by spreadsheet row
> number.** Every specification is keyed by `parameter_key` plus applicability filters.
> The workbook entry number is recorded as provenance only.
